leftEvidence.title: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: After six days Jesus takes three disciples up a high mountain; his face shines, his clothes become white, and Moses and Elijah appear speaking with him.
points.right: After six days Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain and is transfigured before them.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Peter proposes three tents; a bright cloud overshadows them, the voice names the beloved Son and commands listening, and the frightened disciples finally see Jesus alone.
points.right: Elijah and Moses appear speaking with Jesus; Peter proposes tents because he does not know what to say, a cloud overshadows them, and the voice commands listening.

payload.posture: Both preserve six days, three disciples, transformation, Moses and Elijah, tents, cloud, voice, and Jesus alone.

rightEvidence.title: Mark preserves dazzling clothes and Peter’s fear

payload.tension: Matthew emphasizes shining face, bright cloud, prostration, and touch; Mark emphasizes dazzling clothes and Peter’s terror.
payload.title: Matthew and Mark on the mountain
